seo.intro: Two tabs cover the everyday uses of QR codes: generate one from text or a link with custom colours, size, margin and error correction, exporting PNG or SVG, or drop and paste a QR image to read it back as text.
steps: Enter the text or URL and pick an error-correction level (Q or H if it will be printed or handled roughly).
Tune size, margin and colours, then download the PNG, or the SVG when you need a vector.
For the reverse direction, switch to the detect tab and drop, paste or pick a QR image to decode it.

faq.q: Which error-correction level should I use?
faq.a: L recovers about 7% of codewords, M about 15%, Q about 25% and H about 30%. L or M is enough on screen; choose Q or H for print, outdoor use or a logo overlaid in the middle.

faq.q: Why does my recoloured code stop scanning?
faq.a: Readers rely on contrast between modules and background. Too little contrast, or an inverted light-on-dark code, breaks detection — keep a dark foreground on a light background.
No. Detection decodes the image locally in your browser and never sends it anywhere.
